title: How did the dinosaurs disappear?
text: Dinosaurs lived on the Earth for more than one hundred and sixty million years. Then, about sixty-six million years ago, they disappeared. For a long time, scientists did not know why.

In 1980 a team of scientists found a strange thin layer of rock all over the world. It had a lot of iridium, a metal that is rare on the Earth but common in asteroids. They had a new idea: an asteroid hit the Earth.
Later, scientists found the crater in Mexico, near the town of Chicxulub. It is about one hundred and eighty kilometers wide. The asteroid was about ten kilometers wide, as big as a city.

The impact did not kill all the dinosaurs at once. It caused fires, giant waves and huge clouds of dust. The dust covered the sky and the sunlight did not reach the plants. The plants died, the animals that ate plants died, and then the hunters died too.
But not all the dinosaurs disappeared. Some small dinosaurs with feathers survived. Do you know their names today? They are the birds! A chicken is a distant cousin of the [T. rex].
q: How long did dinosaurs live on the Earth?

grammar.title: Grammar: the past simple negative
grammar.rule: For the negative in the past simple, use did not + verb (without -ed). It is the same for all people.
rows: It did not kill all the dinosaurs.
The light did not reach the plants.
items: The impact did not ___ all the dinosaurs.
The sunlight did not ___ the plants.
We did not ___ a living dinosaur.
